learning_outcomes.text: Differentiate and describe the different elements that integrate an electric traction system.
Analyze the operating principle of the types of electric machines used in traction systems as well as their constructive particularities.
Describe and analyze the topology and operating principle of electronic converters used in electric traction systems.
Apply and analyze the fundamentals of control algorithms used in electric traction systems.
Differentiate the industrial application areas of electric traction systems based on their constituent elements and constructive characteristics.
Automate an industrial process using wired logic and programmed logic, based on identifying the operation of the different elements used.
Select the appropriate variable speed drive based on its operating principle, structure, and control strategies for a given industrial application.
Identify incidents that can affect the correct operation of electrical machines, as well as existing detectors and protections on the market.
Choose and calculate the appropriate protection for various electrical machines based on their power, location, type of incident, and the circumstances surrounding an electrical installation.
Write and present a technical report on the application of acquired knowledge about control and protection of machines and installations.

syllabus_topics: Types, operating principles and constructive characteristics of electric machines used in traction systems
Operating principle and constructive characteristics of induction machines
Operating principle and constructive characteristics of permanent magnet synchronous machines
Operating principle and constructive characteristics of reluctance synchronous machines
Modeling of electric machines used in traction systems
Storage systems used in electric traction
Energy management of traction batteries: Charge and discharge behavior
Demand profiles of electric traction applications
Characteristics, properties, and operating principle of power electronic switches
The MOSFET and the power IGBT
Control circuits for power electronic switches
Topology and operating principles of electronic converters used in traction systems
assessment_rules: For the ordinary assessment, the theoretical/practical exam can be between 40% and 70%, the course project between 10% and 30%, and exercises and practice between 10% and 30%. To pass, a minimum of 40% of the maximum score is required in each part of the theoretical/practical exam and in the course project. If the overall grade is 5 or higher but the 40% minimum in the exam or project is not met, the final grade will be 4. For the extraordinary assessment, a theoretical exam (60-80%) and a practical exam (20-40%) are given, requiring a minimum of 40% in each. For differentiated assessment, a theoretical/practical exam (80-90%) and a project (10-20%) are used, with a 40% minimum required in both for passing.
